content.text: : irritate & swelling of nasal mucous membrane
▪︎personal hx of other atopic dz (asthma, eczema, atopic dermatitis) + family hx of allergic rhinitis
▪︎seasonal: spring = flowering shrubs + tree pollen; summer = flowering plants + grasses; fall = ragweeds + molds
▪︎perennial: dust, air pollution, household mites, pet dander
: nonallergic, ⇡ blood flow to nasal mucosa
» idiopathic (MC), temp Δ (ex, cold/dry air, humidity)
» irritants (ex, cigarettes), RX (ex, ASA, NSAIDs), emotions
» ⇡sensitivity of vidian nerve (nerve of pterygoid canal)
▪︎eye sx: clear epiphora, eye irritation, conjunctival erythema, nasal/lacrimal pruritus
pale, boggy nasal mucosa w/ hypertrophic turbinates
cobblestone appearance of posterior pharyngeal wall
: allergy testing (RAST or skin testing if severe/refractory)
▪︎intranasal steroids can take ≥2 wk before Sx relief
▪︎2nd-gen antihistamines can be added to intranasal steroids; temporary but immediate Sx control
▪︎2nd-gen > 1st-gen (ex, diphenhydramine, chlorpheniramine, brompheniramine) d/t less sedation + anticholinergic AEs
▪︎avoidance (⇣exposure to allergens): allergen-free home, air purifiers + dust filters, nasal saline irrigation (flushes allergens)
▪︎refer to allergist for immunotherapy if severe Sx or strong family hx of atopy; ⇣circulating IgE + ⇣need for allergy meds
▪︎assoc w/ nasal polyps, asthma, ASA sensitivity (Samter triad)
▪︎pale, boggy, edematous masses of hypertrophied nasal mucosa; assoc w/ chronic allergic rhinitis
RF: chronic rhinosinusitis, CF (children), ASA exacerbated resp dz (Samter’s triad)
▪︎Samter triad = asthma + aspirin sensitivity + nasal polyps; avoid salicylates → may precipitate severe bronchospasm
: postnasal drip, bilat nasal obstruct, hyposmia/anosmia
Red Flag S/SXS: unilat, young children (CF), unilat epistaxis, facial pain
: topical steroids (drops), monitor growth in children
▪︎small polyps: topical intranasal corticosteroids; short course oral corticosteroids also alleviates Sx of polyps + allergic rhinitis
▪︎large, obstructive or refractory: polypectomy → intranasal corticosteroids after to ⇣recurrence
▪︎severe recurrent polyps or asthma pts at ⇡risk w/ repeated polypectomies → ethmoidectomy
▪︎viral URI (eg common cold) w/ sore throat, rhinorrhea, nasal congestion, + malaise
▪︎etiologies (MC → least): rhinoviruses, unknown, coronaviruses, influenza, RSV, parainfluenza, adenoviruses, enteroviruses, metapneumovirus
: rhinitis + nasal congestion (MC), sore throat, cough, malaise, fever (uncommon in adults, more common in children), conjunctivitis
: supportive care, analgesics (NSAIDs, acetaminophen), antihistamines or decongestants (adults only), intranasal cromolyn (adults only)
▪︎complications: acute rhinosinusitis, lower resp tract dz, asthma exacerbation, AOM
